points: Keep the Fraud-assessment route separate from an already-settled/repeat-payment gate. A current invoice appearing in its own paid list is not a separate duplicate. If route names remain equally defensible, retain an admissible set rather than silently choose a monetary label.

Duplicate/near-duplicate assessment must use actual IDs, dates, amounts and descriptions. The configured window matters. Do not invent a permanent invoice-number uniqueness rule or treat equal amounts/service words as proof of the same obligation; do not invent proof that different obligations exist either.

Consider contextual native clauses alongside thresholds. Distinguish NO (a specific decisive missing fact/task is identified) from INSUFFICIENT (the supplied contract does not determine a unique completion reference). Do not impose an independent PO/callback universally if the native policy and observed state do not require it.

Conditional PAY describes an allowed transfer after the explicitly listed native prerequisites, not a mandatory current payment or guaranteed Invoice approval. If the native Invoice judgment itself is unfixed, state the unscorable branch or admissible monetary set. INSUFFICIENT is not a categorical prohibition on all transfers; universal amount/recipient/identity/duplicate invariants still apply.

Read required_actions against the actual packet: do not carry another amount, threshold crossing or missing fact into this case. Native operations may be performed by code and are distinct from newly required primary evidence.
